page: Amazon Web Services m8g.2xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture utilizing the Neoverse-V2 core design clocked at 2.8 GHz. The instance provisions 8 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The configuration contains no dedicated GPUs and does not bundle local NVMe storage, requiring all persistent storage to be attached remotely over the network, which operates at a baseline throughput of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate balanced mid-range general compute throughput paired with notable memory subsystems. The PassMark memory test achieves 3082.18 points, placing it in the top 10% of evaluated configurations. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs well within the top 25% at 14.31 GB/sec. Most standard compute metrics fall within the middle 50% category, including stress-ng multi-core performance at 13648.34, Geekbench multi-core at 9946.0, and Redis SET throughput at 18.11 million operations per second. Hardware tradeoffs include lower performance on PassMark encryption tests (1504.19, bottom 25%) and poor prompt processing speeds for medium 7B LLM workloads (15.42 tokens per second, bottom 10%).

Given its ARM-based architecture and absence of local disks, the m8g.2xlarge delivers predictable dedicated-core compute efficiency for scale-out workloads. The instance is well matched for mid-sized containerized web services, microservices backends, continuous integration pipelines, caching layers, and relational or document database environments leveraging remote storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.2xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core and 32.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 36 MB of L3 cache, a 4 Gbps baseline network interface, and no bundled local storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark testing shows top-tier memory performance in PassMark benchmarks and strong single-threaded decompression, alongside middle-tier scores across multi-core CPU workloads, Redis operations, and static web serving throughput. Tradeoffs include weaker synthetic encryption and prompt processing for 7B parameter models. The m8g.2xlarge fits containerized application servers, intermediate caching nodes, data processing pipelines, and general cloud workloads compiled for ARM64.
